Relevant to the female superheros in high heels, I have a question. I have at least two relatives who specifically change into high heels in order to dance, often quite energetically. I get the strong impression that this is not for aesthetics, that the high heels make it easier to dance. Is this plausible, and how does it relate to the difficulty of running in high heels mentioned above?

I can't speak for them and don't have dancing experience, but I can't run in heels. It's much more difficult to balance, you can't flex your foot in the same way to push off from the ground, your calf muscles can't move as freely and are therefore less efficient, your ankle muscles are constantly readjusting to keep you upright.

Most of all though it's painful. Much more of your body weight is on the balls of your feet than usual, rather than being evenly distributed over the heel, ball and outer arch. As far as the balls of your feet are concerned, you're putting twice as much pressure on them as you do naturally. This is why women who wear heels when they go out often buy those gel pads for their shoes and still end up taking the shoes off before the end of the night and swapping to a pair of soft flats they keep in their bag, or even going barefoot.

There are treatments you can get nowadays where fillers are injected into the balls of your feet every few months to cushion them, like semi-permanent gel pads. No one would do that if heels didn't hurt.

Ever seen a track athlete competing in heels? Nope, me neither.

posts.name: Julia
posts.cooked:
It really depends on your heels and of course, training. Dancing or running in block heels, for instance, is no biggie, provided they are closed and not a silly sling/open toed deal. While running, you lean forward anyway, so the block actually helps you push off with the ball of your foot. As for dancing, I can't really tell you why, but heels change the way you balance your body, and ballroom, tap etc, actually becomes easier in heels than in flats (Tap dancing in flats is pretty much impossible, actually).

Pointy heels are a different matter, but it is entirely possible to run with them, and run fast at that. Where I live, there is a race at the Pride festival each year, where the contestants run in spikey heels (most of them are dudes), and I have never actually seen someone fall. The actual heel doesn't have contact to the ground when they run anyway, so with a pair of shoes you are comfortable in and some practice, you can run as fast in heels as in sneakers.

So yeah, if you want impossible, try running in flip-flops. Now that is a nightmare!

A few more comments about body types. There is a big difference between "fat" and "thick".  Just because people have a thicker build they are not necessarily fat. Again I would say go look at camille leblanc-bazinet. She won the 2014 crossfit games and I can assure you she is not fat, but she is not skinny either. Can you eat a lot of food and be heavy set and still athletic? Sure. Can you drink beer have a gut and still be athletic? Sure. Will you be able to do what needs to be done to save the world? Probably not. We are talking about superheroes after all. Not just people that are in the top 25% or even in the top 10%.  These are the elite of the elite.

As for running in high heels, sorry those will not help you. If you are a heel strike runner the high heel will break off straight away. If you are a good form runner you won't be able to use your calf in your running motion. There is a reason we race in "flats". The current distance racing shoe has about a 5mm-9mm heel rise. The sprinting shoes are dead flat.

Actually, the argument "these are superheroes" kind of throws the concept of athleticism out the window wholesale. Consider that muscle and tendons can only do so much, super-human strength has nothing to do with muscle mass. neither does superhuman speed, metabolism, agility, flight, energy creation, etc. etc. Why couldn't someone weighing 400lbs and looking like Gabriel Iglesias run 700 MPH and bench press a tank? (actually, that would be pretty awesome) If you say "they're not fit" I would point out that decatheletes can't leap over buildings and fire laser beams out of their ears, obviously something else is going on here. 

 

I can see the argument for Wraith, Fixer, Expat, i.e. the more high tech or costumed crimefighter heroes. but for the characters whose powers surpass anything "human" (legacy, Captain Cosmic, AA, Tempest, SkyScraper, Spite.) why would they have to be fit. 

 

 

EDIT: not to pick on Mr. Iglesias, just the first name that came to mind.
